source_notes: NICE guideline NG252, published 15 October 2025, 145 pages, fully text-extractable, no retraction notice. Purely qualitative consensus document: no printed equations, effect sizes, or unit-bearing quantities; quantitative evidence resides in separate evidence-review documents referenced p. 145 (not in this file). Recommendations 1.1.1-1.12.7 and 1.22.1-1.26.11 explicitly based on qualitative evidence (p. 90). Primitives are faithful predicate-logic formalizations of printed decision rules, explicitly labeled as formalizations (no source equations exist). Open-set caveats recorded where lists are exemplary.

primitives.name: 24-hour postural management conjunctive gate: mobility impairment AND risk presence
primitives.verbatim_quote: Consider 24-hour postural management strategies (for example, regular positional changes, bed positioning, wheelchair and seating systems, arm supports and splints) if the person is: • not able, or is less able, to sit up or stand up unaided or move independently, and • at risk of skin breakdown, pain, sleep disturbance, respiratory dysfunction or muscle or joint contracture.
primitives.latex: \mathrm{Impaired}\big(M_{sit}\lor M_{stand}\lor M_{move}\big)\;\land\;\big(\exists\, r\in\mathcal{R}:\mathrm{AtRisk}(r)\big)\;\Rightarrow\;\mathrm{Consider}\big(\mathrm{PosturalMgmt}_{24h}\big),\quad \mathcal{R}=\{\text{skin breakdown, pain, sleep disturbance, respiratory dysfunction, contracture}\}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: M_sit, M_stand, M_move = unaided sitting/standing/independent-movement capacities [binary predicates, dimensionless 0/1]; Impaired = 'not able, or is less able' graded predicate [0/1 with clinical grading]; AtRisk(r) = risk predicate for factor r [0/1]; R = enumerated risk set (5 factors as printed); PosturalMgmt_24h = 24-hour postural management strategy set (positional changes, bed positioning, wheelchair/seating systems, arm supports, splints) [coverage: 24 hours/day]; Consider = deontic recommendation operator, not obligation [dimensionless]. Logical conjunction is the load-bearing structure; all predicates dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose recommendations, no equations; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic formalization of the printed rule, not a source equation. Recommendation 1.16.8 (p. 49); population: chronic neurological disorders including acquired brain injury (overview p. 7); both bullet conditions must hold simultaneously ('and'); strategies listed are examples ('for example'); recommendation strength is 'consider', based on qualitative evidence and committee consensus (p. 90).
primitives.breakdown_regime: The gate is conjunctive: mobility impairment alone or risk alone does not trigger it - dropping the AND over-triggers (resource waste) or under-triggers (preventable contracture, skin breakdown). 'Less able' is graded, so the Impaired threshold is a clinical judgment, not a measured binary. The risk list is explicit but clinical judgment may extend it. 24-hour coverage presupposes staffing and equipment availability; where unavailable the rule cannot be executed as printed.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the engine's fail-closed protective gates: a conjunctive trigger (capability impairment AND risk exposure) authorizes a protective intervention, exactly the AND-structure of conformal abstention (uncertainty unbounded AND exposure present -> No-Bet). The invariant binds as a constraint on any care or execution transition kernel: protective action requires both legs of the conjunction, never one.
layer2.telemetry: Mobility assessment scores (sit/stand/move); per-factor risk flags in R; postural-management coverage hours per day; incidence of skin breakdown/contracture as gate-failure outcomes. Clinical telemetry only.

primitives.name: Exercise dose as a jointly-agreed constrained vector (frequency, duration, intensity)
primitives.verbatim_quote: agree a clinically relevant exercise dose (frequency, duration and intensity).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D = exercise dose vector; f = frequency [sessions/week]; d = duration [minutes/session]; i = intensity [clinical intensity scale - source does not specify a numeric scale]; C = feasible-dose constraint set conditioned on executive function EF [cognitive capacity, graded], fatigue F_fatigue [graded, fluctuating per pp. 44-45], pain P_pain [graded], risk/harm assessment [0/1 flags], support/supervision level [categorical]; joint agreement = shared-decision constraint [dimensionless]. D has mixed physical units (sessions/week, min/session, intensity scale); C is a state-dependent feasible set, not an objective function - the source prints no optimization target.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose recommendations, no equations; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic formalization of the printed rule, not a source equation. Recommendation 1.15.1 (p. 46): programme developed WITH the person to optimise muscle strength, exercise capacity and physical functioning; must take account of executive function, fatigue, pain, risks/harms, support level; supervised and unsupervised options considered; dose agreed, not prescribed unilaterally. Registered practitioner oversight per 1.15.3 (p. 47).
primitives.breakdown_regime: No numeric dose is printed anywhere in NG252 - the feasible set C is clinician-constructed, so the invariant is the constraint structure, not any particular (f,d,i). Executive-function impairment can invalidate the joint-agreement assumption (capacity). Fatigue and pain fluctuate (pp. 44-45), making C time-varying; a static dose agreed at baseline can leave the feasible set mid-programme. Risk of harmful consequences must be re-evaluated as state changes.

layer2.mapping: Derived constrained-dose kernel for any load scheduler in the 22-agent system (rehabilitation or athletic): the admissible training-load transition is restricted to D in C(state), where the state carries fatigue, pain and cognitive-capacity channels. The kernel binds as a hard feasibility constraint on load transitions - a dose outside C is inadmissible regardless of its projected benefit, mirroring fail-closed certification.
layer2.telemetry: Agreed (f,d,i) per programme block; fatigue/pain/executive-function state time series; supervision level; adherence and dropout; adverse-event flags. Internal clinical/athletic telemetry; no market inputs.

primitives.name: Progressive-condition dose scheduling: low/intermediate frequency over a longer horizon
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the person has a progressive neurological condition, think about low- or intermediate-frequency treadmill gait training over a longer period to optimise their mobility and exercise capacity.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Progressive = progressive neurological condition predicate [0/1]; f = treadmill gait-training frequency [sessions/week]; f_low, f_mid = low/intermediate frequency bands [sessions/week - numeric bounds not printed]; T_long = extended training horizon [weeks to months - not numerically defined]; M_mobility = mobility outcome [clinical scale]; C_exercise = exercise capacity outcome [clinical scale]; Prefer = deontic scheduling preference ('think about'), not mandate. Frequency x horizon is the dose-distribution structure; outcome scales are clinical, dimensionless ordinals.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose recommendations, no equations; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic formalization of the printed rule, not a source equation. Recommendation 1.16.10 (p. 49); applies specifically to progressive conditions (inclusion list pp. 140-143); objective as printed is to optimise mobility AND exercise capacity; treadmill gait training may also improve exercise capacity during the training period and motivate longer-term activity (1.16.9, p. 49).
primitives.breakdown_regime: 'Low', 'intermediate' and 'longer' are undefined numerically - the invariant is the temporal distribution preference (spread dose over time rather than concentrate it), not a specific schedule. Rapidly progressive conditions shorten the effective horizon and can defeat the long-period strategy. Progressive-condition heterogeneity (e.g. motor neurone disease vs primary progressive MS) means the preference is a committee heuristic from qualitative evidence, not an effect-size-derived optimum.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to maintenance-loading schedules for slowly degrading systems: when the underlying capacity declines progressively, distribute stimulus at low/intermediate frequency over a long horizon rather than concentrating a high-frequency block that the system cannot sustain. The same scheduling invariant governs chronic-condition management and long-horizon load maintenance in the engine's athlete models.
layer2.telemetry: Session frequency and horizon length; mobility and exercise-capacity trajectory slopes; retention of capacity after supervised training stops (1.16.12, p. 50).

primitives.name: FES etiological gate: upper-motor-neurone lesion causation conditions stimulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the person has muscle weakness of the lower limbs, caused by an upper motor neurone lesion, consider functional electrical stimulation in addition to gait training.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Weakness_LL = lower-limb muscle weakness predicate [0/1]; Cause(UMN lesion) = etiological predicate: weakness caused by an upper motor neurone lesion [0/1]; UMN = upper motor neurone (central); FES = functional electrical stimulation [intervention, parameters defined in the referenced interventional procedures guidance, not in this file]; + = adjunctive composition ('in addition to'), NOT replacement; GaitTraining = gait training intervention; Consider = deontic recommendation operator [dimensionless]. The gate is etiological: the same symptom (weakness) with a different cause does not satisfy the antecedent.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose recommendations, no equations; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic formalization of the printed rule, not a source equation. Recommendation 1.16.14 (p. 50); explicit cross-reference to NICE interventional procedures guidance on FES for drop foot of central neurological origin; FES is adjunctive to gait training, never a substitute; distinct from 1.16.13 (p. 50) which considers NMES in addition to strengthening and functional activity without the UMN gate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Etiological misclassification breaks the gate: mixed upper/lower motor neurone pathology (e.g. amyotrophic lateral sclerosis) or peripheral neuropathy coexisting with central lesions makes Cause(UMN) ambiguous. The gate is symptom-blind by design - weakness alone never triggers it. Evidence for FES parameters and efficacy lives in the separate interventional procedures guidance, not in NG252; 'consider' is weaker than 'offer'.

layer2.mapping: Derived etiology-conditioned intervention selector: the mechanism channel (lesion type) gates the intervention channel (FES), so identical symptoms route to different actions depending on cause. This is the general operator of mechanism-conditioned selection in the engine - an intervention is admissible only when its causal antecedent is verified, never on symptom match alone.
layer2.telemetry: Weakness localization and severity; lesion classification (UMN/LMN/mixed) with diagnostic provenance; FES adjunct adherence; gait-speed and drop-foot outcomes pre/post.

primitives.name: Fatigue confounder screening: treatable-factor set before primary attribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: Check for treatable factors that may be affecting fatigue, for example, mood difficulties, sleep problems, nutritional problems, abnormal endocrine function, medication and some neurological symptoms, including vestibular problems and sensory symptoms.
primitives.latex: \mathrm{Check}\big(\mathcal{T}\mid F_{obs}\big),\quad \mathcal{T}=\{\text{mood, sleep, nutrition, endocrine, medication, vestibular, sensory}\},\quad t\in\mathcal{T}_{reversible}\Rightarrow\mathrm{Treat}(t)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: F_obs = observed fatigue [graded clinical report, fluctuating best-to-worst per 1.14.2 p. 44]; T = treatable-factor screening set (7 enumerated classes as printed: mood difficulties, sleep problems, nutritional problems, abnormal endocrine function, medication, vestibular problems, sensory symptoms); T_reversible = subset judged reversible/treatable [clinical judgment]; Check = screening operator; Treat = intervention on reversible factor; specialist advice if needed (1.14.4). All predicates dimensionless; the invariant is the screening-set structure, not a quantitative fatigue model.
primitives.assumptions: Source prints prose recommendations, no equations; the LaTeX is a faithful predicate-logic formalization of the printed rule, not a source equation. Recommendation 1.14.4 (p. 45); factor list is exemplary ('for example'), not exhaustive; fatigue assessed at best and worst (1.14.2, p. 44); person's awareness/understanding of fatigue taken into account (1.14.3, pp. 44-45); management integrates pacing/energy conservation, CBT, appropriate physical activity (1.14.7, p. 45).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Factors interact (sleep <-> mood <-> pain <-> medication), so independent screening can miss compound causation; the reversible/irreversible boundary is clinical judgment. Because the list is exemplary, unknown confounders outside T remain un-screened - the same open-set problem as unobserved coverage classes in residualization. Attributing fatigue to the primary neurological condition without screening T inflates the primary attribution, exactly the confounding bias residual metrics are built to remove.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the residualization operator used for ESOE/RYOE in the football engine: before attributing an outcome to the primary cause, screen and remove the reversible confounder set. Fatigue screening is clinical residualization - the primary-condition attribution is only valid after T is checked and treated, just as receiver skill is only isolated after scheme, leverage and timing are conditioned out.
layer2.telemetry: Screening-checklist completion per factor in T; treatments applied and response; fatigue trajectory before/after reversible-factor correction; specialist-referral rate.

reasoning_traces.think: The first discovery of this audit is negative and must be stated plainly: NG252 contains no equations, no effect sizes, and no unit-bearing quantities anywhere in its 145 pages. The quantitative evidence lives in separate evidence-review documents referenced on p. 145 but not included in this file, and the guideline itself states that whole recommendation blocks are based on qualitative evidence (p. 90). A lesser extraction would either fabricate numbers or refuse a perfectly readable source. The honest third path is to recognize that a consensus guideline still encodes sovereign invariants - they are logical, not numerical. The load-bearing example is recommendation 1.16.8 (p. 49): 24-hour postural management is triggered by a conjunction - the person is not able, or less able, to sit, stand or move independently, AND is at risk of skin breakdown, pain, sleep disturbance, respiratory dysfunction, or muscle or joint contracture. The AND is the mathematics. Drop either leg and the rule fails in opposite directions: mobility impairment alone over-triggers a resource-intensive 24-hour regime for people who do not need it, while risk alone under-triggers it for the immobile people who will develop contractures and pressure damage. Those harms are irreversible state transitions - a contracture, once formed, changes the feasible state space of every future rehabilitation transition - which is why the gate is protective and fail-closed in spirit: when both legs hold, inaction is the dangerous branch. This is structurally identical to the conformal abstention gate in the probability-engine dossier: uncertainty unbounded AND exposure present -> abstain. Both are conjunctive certificates guarding a transition, and both derive their force from the asymmetry of the harms they prevent. The deontic operator matters too: NICE writes 'consider', not 'must', and the strategies are examples, not a closed list. The invariant is the gate's logical form and its risk set, not a rigid protocol; a formalization that hardened 'consider' into an obligation would misrepresent the source. The surrounding architecture reinforces the reading: holistic needs assessment (1.8), goal setting with the person (1.9), a single point of contact (1.11), and explicit warnings that interventions can limit recovery if used inappropriately, especially in functional neurological disorder (1.16.7, p. 49). Every one of these is a constraint on transitions, not a prediction. The guideline's mathematics is the algebra of admissible actions under uncertainty, and that algebra is exactly what a fail-closed decision engine needs. Provenance is kept honest throughout: these are committee-consensus rules from qualitative evidence, labeled as such, with the predicate-logic LaTeX presented as formalization of printed prose rather than as source equations.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The lineage runs from NICE's formal-consensus methodology through the qualitative evidence base the committee explicitly acknowledges (p. 90), into the postural-management gate whose risk set - skin breakdown, contracture, respiratory dysfunction - descends from decades of immobility-complication research in spinal cord injury and neurorehabilitation. The hidden state deposited in the rule is the irreversibility of those complications: the gate exists because the harms it prevents cannot be undone by later transitions, which is precisely why the conjunction is protective rather than permissive.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The committee models the clinician under resource pressure: a busy ward will ration 24-hour postural management, so the rule must say exactly when it is warranted, lest it be either diluted to everyone or withheld from the immobile few. The clinician, in turn, models the person's lived experience - 'less able' is graded because the person's own report of capacity fluctuates day to day. And the person models the clinician's intentions: being placed on a 24-hour regime signals severity, which can frighten or reassure. The gate's conjunction is thus a shared-belief device: it aligns three minds on the same trigger conditions, so that protective action is neither a rationing artifact nor an anxiety response, but a certified response to verified impairment plus verified risk.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The tissue-level layer vetoes any optimization that treats postural management as optional cost: skin breakdown and contracture are irreversible transitions, so a policy that skips the gate to save staffing hours trades a bounded present cost for an unbounded future state-space restriction. Conversely, the resource layer vetoes universal application - the conjunction exists to prevent over-triggering. And the deontic layer vetoes hardening: 'consider' preserves clinical judgment for cases the enumerated risk set does not capture. Each veto keeps the gate faithful to the asymmetry of harms that generated it.

reasoning_traces.think: The second cluster of invariants governs dose, cause, and attribution. Recommendation 1.15.1 (p. 46) defines the exercise dose as a triple - frequency, duration, intensity - that must be agreed with the person and must take account of executive function, fatigue, pain, risk, and supervision. The sovereign content is not any numeric dose (none is printed) but the constraint structure: the admissible dose lives in a feasible set conditioned on the person's current state, and that set is time-varying because fatigue and pain fluctuate (pp. 44-45). A static prescription agreed at baseline can leave the feasible set mid-programme; the invariant is the membership constraint D in C(state), which is exactly how a load scheduler should bind training transitions. Recommendation 1.16.10 (p. 49) adds a temporal-distribution invariant: for progressive conditions, prefer low- or intermediate-frequency treadmill training over a longer period to optimise mobility and exercise capacity. The mathematics is dose spreading - when the substrate degrades progressively, concentrate less and sustain longer - and it is isomorphic to maintenance loading for any slowly degrading system. Recommendation 1.16.14 (p. 50) is the sharpest gate: functional electrical stimulation is considered only when lower-limb weakness is CAUSED by an upper motor neurone lesion, and always in addition to gait training. The antecedent is etiological, not symptomatic: identical weakness from a peripheral cause does not satisfy the gate. Mechanism conditions intervention; symptom match alone is never sufficient. This is the clinical form of a principle the football engine also needs - an intervention is admissible only when its causal antecedent is verified. Finally, recommendation 1.14.4 (p. 45) requires screening a treatable-factor set - mood, sleep, nutrition, endocrine, medication, vestibular, sensory - before fatigue is attributed to the primary condition. That is residualization in clinical dress: remove the reversible confounders, then attribute. The parallel to ESOE conditioning out scheme, leverage and timing is exact, and the failure mode is identical - skipping the screen inflates the primary attribution with confounded variance. Two honesty notes close the audit. The factor and strategy lists are exemplary, not closed, so every formalization carries an open-set caveat; and the FND recommendation (1.15.2, pp. 46-47) - goal-oriented movement that acknowledges symptoms while redirecting attention away from them - shows the guideline operating on belief states directly, which is the same lever Coach-Mind pulls when it models what a player attends to under pressure. None of these rules carries a number, and none needs one: their sovereignty is logical, etiological, and attributional, and that is what the artifact records. Note also the deliberate asymmetry between the two stimulation rules: 1.16.13 considers neuromuscular electrical stimulation alongside strengthening and functional activity without any lesion gate, while 1.16.14 reserves functional electrical stimulation for the verified upper-motor-neurone case. The stricter causal antecedent attaches to the more specific intervention - a precision gradient the engine should copy whenever it grades intervention eligibility by the strength of the causal evidence behind it.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The dose-constraint lineage descends from exercise-prescription frameworks (frequency-duration-intensity) filtered through neurorehabilitation's fatigue and executive-function caveats; the behaviour-change list on p. 47 - CBT, self-determination theory, social context theory, motivational interviewing - marks the psychological ancestry of the adherence layer. The FES gate inherits the central-versus-peripheral lesion taxonomy of clinical neurology and the separate NICE interventional procedures guidance on drop foot of central origin. The fatigue screen inherits the biopsychosocial confounder tradition: the hidden state is the discipline of never attributing to the primary disease what a treatable factor could explain.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The FND rule is explicit theory of mind: the therapist acknowledges the symptom's reality while redirecting the person's attention toward the movement goal, because attention to symptoms amplifies them. The person believes the symptom is damage; the therapist believes the symptom is a predictive loop; the intervention changes the belief by changing the attention allocation, not by arguing. In the fatigue screen, the clinician models the person's attribution ('my disease makes me tired') and gently tests alternative causes the person may not have considered - sleep, mood, medication. Both moves are recursive belief engineering under uncertainty, and both succeed only if the person's own model is engaged rather than overridden - which is why the dose is agreed, not prescribed.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The etiological layer vetoes symptom-matching: FES for lower-motor-neurone weakness fails the causal antecedent, so the intervention is inadmissible however well the symptom fits - the mechanism layer refuses the symptom layer's shortcut. The fluctuation layer vetoes static dosing: a dose outside the current feasible set C(state) is inadmissible even if it was agreed last month, because fatigue and pain moved the boundary. And the attribution layer vetoes premature primary-cause claims: fatigue unexplained by the screened treatable set is not yet evidence of primary disease progression. Each veto is a lower layer refusing an upper layer's convenient fiction, the same discipline the engine applies when biomechanics refuses a simulator's phantom stops.

universal_lens: A polymath audit lens: invariants need not be numerical. A qualitative consensus guideline still encodes sovereign structure - conjunctive gates, constrained dose vectors, etiological antecedents, confounder screens. The mathematics is the algebra of admissible transitions under uncertainty; recognizing logical form as a first-class invariant lets clinical consensus and fail-closed engineering certify each other.
gsi_mapping: GSI-native clinical invariants: the 24-hour postural conjunctive gate, the fatigue treatable-factor screen, and the FES upper-motor-neurone etiological gate are directly deployable clinical decision rules with telemetry (mobility scores, risk flags, screening checklists, lesion classification). The constrained exercise-dose vector maps to bioenergetic load management where fatigue and pain make the feasible set time-varying.
gse_mapping: GSE translation: the conjunctive postural gate is isomorphic to fail-closed execution gates; the constrained dose kernel binds athletic load transitions; progressive-condition dose spreading maps to long-horizon maintenance loading; etiological gating generalizes to mechanism-conditioned intervention selection; fatigue screening is clinical residualization parallel to ESOE/RYOE. No sportsbook odds enter any rule; artifacts remain internal and the engine never publishes.
